class good_to_know.forms.ArticleForm(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: ModelForm

Provide a form for creating and editing news articles.

Extends Django’s ModelForm to handle article creation and editing by journalists and editors.

The form allows users to enter an article title and content, upload an optional image and select an associated publisher.

Publisher selection is controlled according to the user’s role.

Journalists can only select publishers with which they are affiliated. Publisher selection is optional for journalists, allowing independent publication.

Editors can only select publishers assigned to their accounts. Publisher selection is mandatory for editors.

class good_to_know.forms.EditorRegistrationForm(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: UserCreationForm

Provide a registration form for editor accounts.

Extends Django’s UserCreationForm to support editor registration.

The form collects the username, email address and password confirmation fields required to create an editor account.

Editors can associate their accounts with existing publishers or register a new publisher during account creation.

Multiple existing publishers can be selected. Alternatively, a new publisher can be created by providing its name and an optional description.

The form prevents editors from selecting existing publishers and creating a new publisher simultaneously.

Publisher names are checked to prevent duplicate registrations.

New publisher names are stripped of surrounding whitespace and checked against existing publisher records to prevent duplicate names.

save(commit=True)[source]

Create and save an editor account and publisher associations.

Uses the parent UserCreationForm save method to create the user instance without immediately saving it.

Assigns the editor role to the user.

If commit is disabled, returns the unsaved user instance.

Otherwise, the method either associates the editor with the selected existing publishers or creates a new publisher using the supplied name and description.

The editor account is then saved and associated with the relevant publishers through the many-to-many relationship.

The transaction ensures that the database operations are performed atomically.

Parameters:

commit (bool) – Determines whether the user instance and publisher associations are saved to the database.

Returns:

The newly created editor user instance.

Return type:

Provide a registration form for journalist accounts.

Extends Django’s UserCreationForm to support journalist registration.

The form collects the username, email address and password confirmation fields required to create a journalist account.

Journalists can optionally associate their accounts with multiple publishers during registration. Independent journalists can leave the publisher selection blank.

Publisher affiliations are stored using the user model’s many-to-many relationship.

class good_to_know.forms.NewsletterForm(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: ModelForm

Provide a form for creating and editing newsletters.

Extends Django’s ModelForm to support newsletter creation and editing by journalists and editors.

Users can provide a newsletter title and description, select an associated publisher and include multiple articles.

Available publishers and articles are filtered according to the authenticated user’s role.

Journalists can select publishers with which they are affiliated and include approved articles written by themselves or associated with their affiliated publishers.

Independent journalists can create newsletters using their own approved articles without selecting a publisher.

Editors can only select publishers assigned to their accounts and include approved articles belonging to those publishers.

The form also validates that all selected articles belong to the selected publisher when a publisher is specified.

Articles contain written content and may optionally include an uploaded image.

Each article has a journalist author and can optionally be associated with a publisher.

Publisher-affiliated articles require editorial approval. Independent articles can be approved without publisher affiliation.

class good_to_know.models.CustomUser(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: AbstractUser

Represent a user account with role-based access control.

Extends Django’s AbstractUser model to support three application roles: readers, editors and journalists.

Each role has different permissions and relationships with publishers and other users.

Readers can subscribe to publishers and journalists. Journalists can belong to publishers and create publications. Editors can be assigned to publishers and manage their content.

Role-based permissions are automatically assigned through Django groups whenever a user account is saved.

assign_group_permissions(group)[source]

Assign application permissions according to the user role.

Defines the Django model permissions available to readers, journalists and editors.

Permissions are retrieved using their associated content types and permission codenames.

The resulting permissions are assigned to the supplied Django group, replacing its existing permission assignments.

Reader permissions provide access to view publications.

Journalist permissions additionally allow article creation, editing and deletion, together with newsletter creation and editing.

Editor permissions provide publication management capabilities, including publisher management.

Parameters:

group (Group) – The Django authentication group receiving the role-specific permissions.

Returns:

None.

Return type:

None

Validate user role and associated relationships.

Ensures that users only maintain publisher relationships and subscription relationships appropriate to their role.

The validation rules prevent:

  • Readers from belonging to journalist or editor publishers.

  • Journalists from belonging to editor publishers or maintaining reader subscription relationships.

  • Editors from belonging to journalist publishers or maintaining reader subscription relationships.

Raises:

ValidationError – If the user has relationships that are incompatible with their assigned role.

None.

save(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Save the user and synchronise role-based permissions.

Performs the save operation within an atomic database transaction.

Before saving, the user account undergoes full model validation. The appropriate Django group is then retrieved or created according to the user’s assigned role.

Any other application role groups are removed before the appropriate group is assigned.

Finally, the permissions associated with the user’s role are synchronised with the assigned group.

Parameters:

  • args – Additional positional arguments passed to the parent model save method.

  • kwargs – Additional keyword arguments passed to the parent model save method.

Returns:

None.

Return type:

None

Bases: Model

Represent a curated collection of news articles.

Newsletters allow journalists to group multiple articles into a single publication.

Each newsletter has a title, description, creation date and journalist or editor author.

Newsletters can optionally be associated with a publisher and contain multiple articles through a many-to-many relationship.

good_to_know.views.api_approve_newsletter(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Approve a newsletter associated with an editor’s publisher.

Allows authenticated editors to approve newsletters belonging to publishers assigned to their accounts.

The newsletter is retrieved using its unique identifier and filtered against the editor’s assigned publishers.

Following successful retrieval, the newsletter’s approval status is updated and saved to the database.

Access is restricted to authenticated users with the editor role. Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

  • request (Request) – The authenticated API request.

  • newsletter_id (int) – The unique identifier of the newsletter to approve.

Raises:

DRFPermissionDenied – If the authenticated user is not an editor or does not have an assigned publisher.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing a confirmation message, the newsletter ID, its title and approval status.

Return type:

Response

good_to_know.views.api_approved_article(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Receive and verify an approved article.

Retrieves an article using the article ID supplied in the API request and verifies that the article has received editorial approval.

If the article exists and is approved, a successful response is returned containing its ID and title.

Access is restricted to authenticated users. Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

request (Request) – The authenticated API request containing the article ID.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing a confirmation message, the article ID and its title.

Return type:

Response

Raises:

Http404 – If the article does not exist or has not received editorial approval.

good_to_know.views.api_article_detail(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Retrieve, update or delete an individual article.

Provides three API operations depending on the HTTP request method.

  • GET: Retrieves an individual article. Approved articles are accessible to all authenticated users. Unapproved articles are restricted to their journalist author or an editor associated with the article’s publisher.

  • PUT: Allows journalists and editors to update articles according to their respective permissions. Journalists can only update their own articles, whereas editors can update articles associated with their assigned publishers.

  • DELETE: Allows journalists to delete their own articles and editors to delete articles associated with their assigned publishers.

Journalist updates preserve article ownership and apply the appropriate approval status according to publisher affiliation. Editor updates preserve publisher ownership and return the article to pending approval.

Model validation is performed before updates are saved. Database transactions are used when saving changes.

Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

  • request (Request) – The authenticated API request containing the HTTP method and, for PUT requests, the submitted article data.

  • article_id (int) – The unique identifier of the article to retrieve, update or delete.

Raises:

DRFPermissionDenied – If the authenticated user does not have permission to access, update or delete the requested article.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing serialized article data, a success message, or serializer validation errors.

Return type:

Response

good_to_know.views.api_articles(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Retrieve approved articles or create a new article.

Provides two API operations depending on the HTTP request method.

  • GET: Retrieves all approved articles, including their associated authors and publishers. Articles are ordered by creation date, with the most recent displayed first.

  • POST: Allows authenticated journalists to create articles. The submitted article is validated using the article serializer and Django model validation.

Articles associated with a publisher require editorial approval. Independent articles are automatically approved. Journalists can only submit articles associated with publishers to which they belong.

Article creation is performed within an atomic database transaction.

Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

request (Request) – The authenticated API request containing the HTTP method and, for POST requests, the submitted article data.

Raises:

DRFPermissionDenied – If the authenticated user is not a journalist when submitting an article, or if the journalist does not belong to the selected publisher.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing serialized article data, serializer validation errors, or the created article.

Return type:

Response

good_to_know.views.api_get_articles(request, **filters)[source]

Retrieve and validate articles submitted through an API request.

Retrieves article IDs from the request data and validates that they are supplied as a list without duplicate entries.

Articles are retrieved from the database using the supplied IDs and any additional filtering criteria. A validation exception is raised if the number of retrieved articles does not match the number of submitted IDs.

Parameters:

  • request (Request) – The API request containing the submitted article IDs.

  • filters (dict) – Additional filtering criteria applied to the article database query.

Raises:

ValidationError – If the article IDs are not supplied as a list, contain duplicates, or include unavailable articles.

Returns:

A queryset containing the validated articles.

Return type:

QuerySet

user (CustomUser) – The authenticated user whose editor role and publisher associations are being checked.

Raises:

DRFPermissionDenied – If the user is not an editor or has no assigned publisher.

QuerySet

good_to_know.views.api_newsletter_detail(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Retrieve an individual newsletter.

Retrieves a newsletter using its unique identifier, including its associated author, publisher and articles.

Access permissions depend on the newsletter’s approval status:

  • Approved newsletters are available to all authenticated users.

  • Unapproved newsletters are restricted to the journalist who created them or editors assigned to the newsletter’s associated publisher.

If an authenticated user does not meet the access requirements for an unapproved newsletter, a REST framework permission exception is raised.

Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

  • request (Request) – The authenticated API request.

  • newsletter_id (int) – The unique identifier of the newsletter to retrieve.

Raises:

DRFPermissionDenied – If the authenticated user does not have permission to access an unapproved newsletter.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing the serialized newsletter data.

Return type:

Response

good_to_know.views.api_newsletters(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Retrieve all approved newsletters.

Retrieves all newsletters that have received editorial approval.

The associated authors, publishers and articles are also retrieved to support newsletter serialization efficiently.

Newsletters are ordered by creation date, with the most recent displayed first.

This endpoint is available to all authenticated users, regardless of their assigned application role.

Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

request (Request) – The authenticated API request.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing the serialized collection of approved newsletters.

Return type:

Response

good_to_know.views.api_publishers(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Retrieve all publishers registered in the application.

Retrieves all publishers from the database and orders them alphabetically by name.

The publisher records are serialized using the publisher serializer before being returned as an API response.

This endpoint is available to all authenticated users, regardless of their assigned application role.

Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

request (Request) – The authenticated API request.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing the serialized list of publishers.

Return type:

Response

good_to_know.views.api_subscribed_articles(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Retrieve approved articles from a reader’s subscriptions.

Retrieves approved articles written by journalists or published by publishers to which the authenticated reader has subscribed.

The results include associated authors and publishers and are ordered by creation date, with the most recent articles displayed first. Duplicate results are removed.

Access is restricted to authenticated users with the reader role. Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

request (Request) – The authenticated API request.

Raises:

DRFPermissionDenied – If the authenticated user does not have the reader role.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing the serialized subscribed articles.

Return type:

Response

good_to_know.views.api_users(request, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Retrieve readers subscribed to an editor’s publisher.

Allows authenticated editors to retrieve a list of readers subscribed to a specified publisher assigned to their account.

The publisher ID must be supplied as a query parameter. The requested publisher is checked against the editor’s assigned publishers before subscriber information is retrieved.

Only users with the reader role who are subscribed to the specified publisher are included in the results.

The returned users are ordered alphabetically by username and serialized using the user serializer.

Access is restricted to authenticated users with the editor role. Authentication is provided through token authentication.

Parameters:

request (Request) – The authenticated API request containing the publisher ID as a query parameter.

Raises:

DRFPermissionDenied – If the authenticated user is not an editor, has no assigned publishers, or attempts to access a publisher outside their assigned publishers.

Returns:

A REST framework response containing the serialized list of subscribed readers or an error message if the publisher ID is not supplied.

Return type:

Response

good_to_know.views.api_validate_model(instance)[source]

Validate a Django model instance and return validation errors.

Runs Django’s full model validation using the full_clean() method. If validation fails, the resulting Django validation errors are converted into Django REST framework validation exceptions for consistent API error handling.

Parameters:

instance (Model) – The Django model instance to validate.

Raises:

ValidationError – If the model instance fails validation.

Returns:

None.

Return type:

None

good_to_know.views.approve_article(request, article_id)[source]

Approve an article and initiate its distribution.

Allows authenticated editors to approve articles associated with their assigned publishers.

Once approved, the article is saved and the distribution process is initiated. Approved articles are distributed to subscribers by email and submitted to the approved articles API.

If distribution fails, the error is recorded in the application log and a warning message is displayed. The article remains approved even if distribution encounters a problem.

The approval operation is restricted to POST requests.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP POST request received from the authenticated editor.

  • article_id (int) – The unique identifier of the article to approve.

Returns:

A redirect response to the editor dashboard.

Return type:

HttpResponseRedirect

good_to_know.views.approve_newsletter(request, newsletter_id)[source]

Approve a newsletter associated with an editor’s publisher.

Allows authenticated editors to approve newsletters associated with their assigned publishers.

The newsletter approval status is updated and saved to the database. Following successful approval, a confirmation message is displayed and the editor is redirected to the editor dashboard.

The approval operation is restricted to POST requests.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP POST request received from the authenticated editor.

  • newsletter_id (int) – The unique identifier of the newsletter to approve.

Returns:

A redirect response to the editor dashboard.

Return type:

HttpResponseRedirect

good_to_know.views.article_detail(request, article_id)[source]

Display the details of an individual article.

Retrieves an article using its ID and displays its details to authenticated users.

Approved articles are accessible to all authenticated users. Unapproved articles can only be accessed by their journalist author or an editor associated with the article’s publisher. Users without the required permissions are denied access.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP request received from the authenticated user.

  • article_id (int) – The unique identifier of the article.

Raises:

PermissionDenied – If the user does not have permission to access an unapproved article.

Returns:

A rendered response containing the article details.

Return type:

HttpResponse

request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP request received from the user.

good_to_know.views.create_article(request)[source]

Create a new article.

Allows authenticated journalists to create articles using the article submission form.

Articles can be submitted independently or associated with a publisher. Articles associated with a publisher require editorial approval, whereas independent articles are automatically approved.

Following successful submission, the journalist is redirected to their dashboard.

Parameters:

request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP request received from the authenticated journalist.

Returns:

A redirect response following successful article creation, or a rendered response containing the article submission form.

Return type:

HttpResponse

good_to_know.views.create_newsletter(request)[source]

Create a new newsletter.

Allows authenticated journalists to create newsletters using the newsletter submission form.

Both independent journalists and journalists affiliated with publishers can create newsletters using their own articles. Newsletters associated with a publisher require editorial approval, whereas independent newsletters are automatically approved.

Newsletter creation and the association of articles are performed within an atomic database transaction.

Following successful creation, the journalist is redirected to the newsletter detail page. If an exception occurs during creation, an error message is displayed.

Parameters:

request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP request received from the authenticated journalist.

Returns:

A redirect response following successful newsletter creation, or a rendered response containing the newsletter submission form.

Return type:

HttpResponse

good_to_know.views.create_publisher(request)[source]

Create a new publisher.

Allows authenticated editors with the required publisher creation permission to create a publisher.

The submitted publisher name is validated to ensure that it is not empty or already in use. Publisher creation is performed within an atomic database transaction, and the newly created publisher is associated with the editor.

Success and error messages are displayed according to the outcome of the operation. If an exception occurs, the failure is recorded in the application log.

Parameters:

request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP request received from the authenticated editor.

Returns:

A redirect response following successful creation, or a rendered response containing the publisher creation form.

Return type:

HttpResponse

Delete an existing article.

Allows authenticated journalists to delete articles that they have authored. The article is retrieved using its unique identifier and the authenticated user’s ownership.

The deletion operation is restricted to POST requests. Following successful deletion, a confirmation message is displayed and the journalist is redirected to their dashboard.

A redirect response to the journalist dashboard.

HttpResponseRedirect

The deletion operation is restricted to POST requests. Following successful deletion, a confirmation message is displayed and the journalist is redirected to their dashboard.

A redirect response to the journalist dashboard.

Return type:

HttpResponseRedirect

good_to_know.views.distribute_approved_article(article, request)[source]

Distribute an approved article to subscribers and the API.

Checks whether the article has been approved before initiating distribution. Approved articles are distributed to readers subscribed to the article’s publisher and journalist.

Subscriber email addresses are collected and used to send an email containing the article as an HTML attachment.

The approved article is also submitted to the application’s approved articles API using token authentication.

If the article has not been approved, the function returns without performing any distribution operations.

Parameters:

  • article (Article) – The article to distribute to subscribers and the approved articles API.

  • request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP request used to construct the API endpoint URL and obtain the authenticated user’s token.

Returns:

None.

Return type:

None

Raises:

  • requests.exceptions.RequestException – If the API request fails or returns an unsuccessful HTTP status code.

  • Exception – If an error occurs during email generation, delivery or API distribution.

Subscribe a reader to a journalist.

Allows authenticated readers to subscribe to journalists.

The journalist is retrieved using their unique identifier, with an additional check to ensure that the account has the journalist role. The journalist is then added to the authenticated reader’s subscribed journalists.

A confirmation message is displayed following successful subscription.

The operation is restricted to POST requests and is only available to authenticated users with the reader role.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP POST request received from the authenticated reader.

  • journalist_id (int) – The unique identifier of the journalist to subscribe to.

Returns:

A redirect response to the home page.

HttpResponseRedirect

Subscribe a reader to a publisher.

Allows authenticated readers to subscribe to publishers.

The publisher is retrieved using its unique identifier and added to the authenticated reader’s subscribed publishers. A confirmation message is displayed following successful subscription.

The operation is restricted to POST requests and is only available to authenticated users with the reader role.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP POST request received from the authenticated reader.

  • publisher_id (int) – The unique identifier of the publisher to subscribe to.

Returns:

A redirect response to the reader dashboard.

Return type:

HttpResponseRedirect

good_to_know.views.unsubscribe_journalist(request, journalist_id)[source]

Unsubscribe a reader from a journalist.

Allows authenticated readers to unsubscribe from journalists to which they have previously subscribed.

The journalist is retrieved using their unique identifier, with an additional check to ensure that the account has the journalist role. The journalist is then removed from the authenticated reader’s subscribed journalists.

A confirmation message is displayed following successful unsubscription.

The operation is restricted to POST requests and is only available to authenticated users with the reader role.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP POST request received from the authenticated reader.

  • journalist_id (int) – The unique identifier of the journalist to unsubscribe from.

Returns:

A redirect response to the reader dashboard.

Return type:

HttpResponseRedirect

Unsubscribe a reader from a publisher.

Allows authenticated readers to unsubscribe from publishers to which they have previously subscribed.

The publisher is retrieved using its unique identifier and removed from the authenticated reader’s subscribed publishers. A confirmation message is displayed following successful unsubscription.

The operation is restricted to POST requests and is only available to authenticated users with the reader role.

Parameters:

  • request (HttpRequest) – The HTTP POST request received from the authenticated reader.

  • publisher_id (int) – The unique identifier of the publisher to unsubscribe from.

A redirect response to the reader dashboard.
